source.title: P-Matchings in Graphs: A Brief Survey with Some Open Problems

accepted.question_text: A disconnected matching in a graph G is a matching M such that either |M| = 1 or the subgraph induced by the matched edges is disconnected. Let βdc(G) denote the maximum size of a disconnected matching in G. What is the computational complexity of determining βdc(G) for an input graph G?

evidence.quote: Example 3.5 (Disconnected matching). A matching M is disconnected if |M| = 1 or <M> is disconnected. We have βdc(G) = max{|M| : M is disconnected matching}
Of the matching varieties discussed in Section 3, this leaves only the complexity of βdc in question.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a property of graphs. If M is a matching in a graph G such that the induced subgraph <M> has property P, call M a P-matching. Define βP(G) = max{|M| : <M> has property P} and β−P(G) = min{|M| : <M> is maximal with respect to P}. For each of the matching classes introduced in the survey, what useful upper bounds can be proved for βP(G), and what useful lower bounds can be proved for β−P(G)?

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1. Let P be a property of G, and let M a matching of G such that the induced subgraph of M, <M>, has property P, then we call M a P-matching. With regard to P-matchings, we are interested in two parameters: βP = max{|M| : <M> has property P} β−P = min{|M| : <M> is maximal with respect to P}.
Of course the first direction would be to find good upper bounds on βP and good lower bounds on β−P for each of the P-matchings introduced here.

accepted.question_text: For a graph property P, call a matching M in G a P-matching when the induced subgraph <M> has property P, and let βP(G) be the largest size of such a matching. For each matching class introduced in the survey, give characterization theorems that decide exactly when a given matching M is a maximum P-matching, meaning that |M| = βP(G).

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1. Let P be a property of G, and let M a matching of G such that the induced subgraph of M, <M>, has property P, then we call M a P-matching.
Also for each P-matching, characterization theorems should be developed to describe when a given matching M is a maximum P-matching.

accepted.question_text: Can one define, for each matching class P considered in the survey, a graph parameter αP(G) that extends the Gallai-type relation for ordinary matchings and satisfies βP(G) + αP(G) = |V(G)| for every graph G?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.4 (Gallai Identities (1959)). If G has no isolates, then i) α0(G)+β0(G) = |V(G)| ii) α1(G)+β1(G) = |V(G)|
Recalling the Gallai identities, it would be of interest to find a parameter, say “αP” such that βP(G)+αP(G) = |V(G)|.

accepted.question_text: For each matching class P considered in the survey, determine sharp Nordhaus-Gaddum-type bounds for βP on a graph G and its complement Ḡ; specifically, find the best possible lower and upper bounds for βP(G) + βP(Ḡ) and for βP(G) · βP(Ḡ).

accepted.question_text: For the various matching classes introduced in the survey, determine the computational complexity of computing βP(G), where βP(G) is the maximum size of a matching in G belonging to the class P.

evidence.quote: With regard to P-matchings, we are interested in two parameters: βP = max{|M| : <M> has property P}
In addition to many other results which could be of interest concerning these parameters, determining the complexity of finding βP is most desirable.
